title: mobile_scanner
objectives: Understand mobile_scanner via a real-life analogy
Configure controller for formats + camera facing + torch
Overlay a scan rectangle + haptics on detect
Optimize CPU + battery for continuous scanning
Handle GS1 / DataMatrix / QR variants correctly

sections.markdown:
**Think of `mobile_scanner` as a specialized barcode reader you wire into your Flutter app.**

It's the `camera` plugin + Google's ML Kit Barcode Scanning wired together with a Flutter widget. You point it at codes; it fires callbacks with what it found.

- **Formats** — 1D (Code 128, EAN-13, UPC-A) + 2D (QR, DataMatrix, PDF417, GS1 DataBar). Choose which to detect — narrower list = faster.
- **Continuous vs one-shot** — keep scanning until you decide to stop, or capture the first hit.
- **Camera controls** — front / back, torch, zoom, focus.
- **Overlay UI** — draw a scan rectangle, corner markers, a moving reticle in Flutter, on top of the camera preview.
- **Debouncing** — same barcode fires many times per second in continuous mode; you must debounce.

**Why every commerce / logistics / delivery Flutter app installs it:** barcode scanning is table-stakes in retail + warehousing. `mobile_scanner` combines the camera-plugin lifecycle care + ML Kit detection into one widget-based API. Same author as some of the other big Flutter plugins; well-maintained.

**`mobile_scanner`** wraps native camera streams + Google **ML Kit Barcode Scanning** on Android + iOS. `MobileScannerController` (formats, cameraFacing, torchEnabled, detectionSpeed, detectionTimeoutMs, returnImage). `MobileScanner` widget with `onDetect` callback receiving `BarcodeCapture` (raw value, format, rawBytes, corners). Alternative: `pod_player`-like preview + your own overlay UI.
## Formats supported

rows: GS1 DataMatrix on pharma, boarding passes
QR / DataMatrix with structured GS1 payload

sections.markdown: ## Full setup
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Not disposing controller.** Camera stays open → next screen can't open. Always `dispose`.
**Mistake 2: No debounce.** Continuous scan fires 30 times a second for the same code; app pops the same route 30 times. Use `DetectionSpeed.noDuplicates` OR de-dup manually by `_lastCode`.
**Mistake 3: All formats enabled.** ML Kit tries every format on every frame — slow. Restrict to what you actually scan.
**Mistake 4: `returnImage: true` always on.** Ships every frame back as bytes — memory pressure. Only true when you need raw.
**Mistake 5: Ignoring lifecycle.** Stopping the scanner on background + resuming on foreground is essential; else 'camera in use' or battery drain.
**Mistake 6: Missing NSCameraUsageDescription / manifest.** Silent iOS failure; Android runtime crash.

**Mistake 7: Small scan rectangle overlay AT WRONG SIZE.** Users think the rectangle IS the scan area; ML Kit actually scans the full frame. Either enforce region-of-interest (feature-gated) or make the overlay just a UX guide.
**Mistake 8: Not handling `LICENSE_UNAVAILABLE`.** Google Play Services may lack ML Kit modules on some devices; catch + fallback.
## Best practices
**1. Narrow the `formats` list** — fastest detection.
**2. `DetectionSpeed.noDuplicates`** for scan-once UX.
**3. Haptic + audio feedback** on detect — great UX.
**4. Torch button** for low-light.
**5. Overlay UX guide** (rectangle / reticle) even if it doesn't limit detection.
**6. Lifecycle-safe start/stop.**
**7. Fallback to typed entry** — some users can't focus (broken camera, low-light); allow manual entry.
**8. Consider `google_mlkit_barcode_scanning`** if you already integrate ML Kit for other tasks; skip mobile_scanner + use camera plugin directly.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — QR-only scanner returning the value on detect.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Multi-format (QR + EAN-13 + DataMatrix); overlay rectangle.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Torch + camera switch + zoom control.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Continuous inventory scan: keep scanning + list all uniques in a session.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — GS1 DataMatrix parser: split raw value into AI-based fields (GTIN, batch, expiry).
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Lifecycle + license fallback: scanner unavailable → fallback to manual entry UI.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What's under the hood + how does it differ from raw ML Kit?**

**A:** `mobile_scanner` combines: (1) the `camera` plugin's preview + frame-streaming pipeline; (2) `google_mlkit_barcode_scanning` for detection; (3) a Dart widget wrapper for the callback + overlay-ready UI. **Advantages over raw ML Kit + camera plugin:** (a) one widget instead of manual `startImageStream` → convert → detect → throttle wiring; (b) built-in lifecycle handling; (c) format restriction as a controller property; (d) `DetectionSpeed.noDuplicates` deduping. **Cost:** less control over the pipeline. **When to use raw ML Kit:** you already stream camera frames for other CV (face detection, text OCR); reuse the same stream + save memory. Interviewers score highly on knowing both paths exist.

**Q2: How do you prevent 'ghost duplicate' pop-ups from continuous scan?**

**A:** ML Kit fires callbacks per-frame — 15-30 fps × same barcode = 15-30 duplicates. **Options:** (1) `DetectionSpeed.noDuplicates` — plugin dedups the same rawValue over a short window. (2) Manual — hold `_lastCode + _lastAt`; ignore if `raw == last && now - lastAt < 800 ms`. (3) One-shot mode — call `_ctrl.stop()` on first detect; user taps 'Scan again' to resume. (4) Session mode — keep a `Set<String>` of scanned codes; ignore repeats. **Which pattern for which UX:** one-shot for 'scan and confirm' (checkout); session-set for 'batch inventory' (warehouse). Interviewers respect a specific pattern, not just 'we debounce.'

**Q3: How do you decode GS1 DataMatrix codes (pharma, food)?**

**A:** GS1 uses **Application Identifiers (AIs)** — 2-4-digit prefixes marking each field. Example raw: `(01)09501234567890(17)230101(10)ABC(21)12345` → GTIN 09501234567890, expiry 2023-01-01, batch ABC, serial 12345. The RAW value from mobile_scanner is a string; you parse via a GS1 AI table. **`mobile_scanner` doesn't parse AIs for you** — use a helper like `gs1_barcode_parser` or roll your own. **Special separator:** GS1 uses `<GS>` (ASCII 29) between variable-length AIs; sometimes rendered as `\u{1d}` in the raw. **Digital Link** — GS1's URL-encoded format (`https://id.gs1.org/01/09501234567890/17/230101/...`) — parse via URL semantics. **Compliance:** pharma / medical device apps in EU + India MUST decode + validate GS1 AIs per DSCSA / DPDPA regulations. Interviewers in retail / logistics love GS1 depth.

**Q4: How do you get high accuracy in low light or on damaged codes?**

**A:** **(1) Torch on** — `_ctrl.toggleTorch()`; UX button. **(2) Auto-exposure lock** on the scan region — some plugins expose; native path via camera plugin. **(3) Zoom in** — for small codes; `_ctrl.setZoomScale(2.0)`. **(4) Higher camera resolution** — `cameraResolution: Size(1920, 1080)` for tiny codes; costs perf. **(5) Multi-format restriction** — narrower list, more CPU per format = better tolerance. **(6) Multiple frames + voting** — some codes need 3-5 detections to be confident; hold state. **(7) DataMatrix > QR for damaged** — DataMatrix has better error correction levels; recommend it when your app controls both ends. **(8) UI guidance** — 'hold still, zoom closer' hints. **When accuracy really matters** (pharma, industrial), consider `scandit` — commercial SDK with better damaged-code handling.

**Q5: How would you build a warehouse inventory scanner UX?**

**A:** **(1) Session mode** — user starts a session; scans codes one after another; `Set<String>` deduplicates within session. **(2) Confirmation + delete** — each scan appears in a list; tap to delete accidentally scanned. **(3) Visual + audio + haptic confirmation** — user knows each scan registered without looking. **(4) Format hint** — probable barcode format for inventory (Code 128); pre-restrict formats. **(5) Torch toggle + camera switch** for varying lighting. **(6) Auto-focus + zoom** for warehouse-height labels. **(7) Sync outbox** — write each scan to a local DB; upload via Workmanager when connectivity returns. **(8) Offline-first** — session survives app crash / reboot; resume where left off. **(9) Barcode-to-product lookup** offline — bundle a partial product catalog. This is a classic Flutter senior interview: knowing the offline + session-mode combo is the differentiator.

**Q6: When would you upgrade from `mobile_scanner` to `scandit`?**

**A:** **`mobile_scanner`** covers 80 % of use cases free + open-source (ML Kit under the hood). **Upgrade to Scandit when:** **(1)** Enterprise-grade accuracy — damaged / low-contrast / oddly-lit codes; Scandit's CV models handle much better. **(2)** Multi-code capture — scan 5 codes at once (shipping labels, pallet manifests). **(3)** Text recognition alongside barcodes (VIN, price tags). **(4)** MatrixScan (AR-style multi-code highlighting). **(5)** Enterprise SLA + support contract. **Cost:** Scandit is paid — licensing per app + per active user. Free tier for < 5000 devices in some plans. **Trade-offs:** Scandit's SDK is bigger (~10 MB APK bloat); mobile_scanner is svelte. **Rule:** stay free until user complaints about scan-fail rates cost more than a Scandit license. Interviewers respect the pragmatic cost-benefit answer.

## Real-world usage

- **Retail POS + inventory scan** — Code 128, EAN, UPC.
- **Warehousing** — Code 128 on pallet labels; GS1 SSCC.
- **Pharma / medical device** — GS1 DataMatrix with lot + expiry.
- **Boarding passes** — Aztec / PDF417.
- **Consumer QR** — payment, deep-links.
- **NOT ideal for** — high-volume industrial scanning with degraded codes (Scandit / Cognex).

## Advanced notes

- **Region-of-interest (ROI)** — some plugin versions expose; else Region isn't limited (ML Kit scans whole frame).
- **`DetectionSpeed.normal`** vs `unrestricted` vs `noDuplicates` — trade-offs.
- **`detectionTimeoutMs`** — throttle callback rate.
- **`returnImage: true`** — bytes attached; huge memory cost; use only for evidence capture.
- **Multiple barcodes per frame** — `BarcodeCapture.barcodes` is a list.
- **Corners** — `Barcode.corners` — 4 points; overlay a bounding box.
- **Camera zoom** — `_ctrl.setZoomScale(1.0-max)`.
- **Pause / resume** — `_ctrl.stop()` / `.start()`.
- **`cameraResolution`** — higher = better distant scan; costs perf.
- **Sound / haptic** — `HapticFeedback.mediumImpact()` on detect.
- **Test on real hardware** — emulators can't scan; use Xcode's simulator with a photo of a barcode as a test hack (limited).
- **Alternatives** — `qr_code_scanner` (older, ZXing-based); `google_mlkit_barcode_scanning` (raw ML Kit).
